newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow drop drives down Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow drop drives down Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market trailed the Dow lower at the opening on Wednesday with across-the-board losses exacerbated by the Reserve Bank of Australia's apparent decision to leave official interest rates unchanged.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index shed 11.1 points to 2,369.0.

Brokers said with bond markets slipping and a weaker Wall Street, there was little to excite positive interest among investors as they contemplated current interest rates and a volatile Australian dollar and metals prices.
"There is no real reason to take a positive view today although the fall could have been worse," said a Sydney broker, pointing to the smaller proportional losses on the local bourse.
Miner WMC and ANZ Bank led the turnover lists early with brokers saying options-related activity prior to the markets' official dominating trade in those stocks.
At the smaller end, Bligh Oil shares were fuelled by Tuesday's announcement of a gas find in Texas in the United States.
Bligh scrip leapt 48 percent to A$0.51 (US$0.41) early before settling about 30 percent higher.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of two to one, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
